newsitem.title: KUWAIT: Kuwait paper slams U.S. over China gun deal.
newsitem.headline: Kuwait paper slams U.S. over China gun deal.

text.p: A leading Kuwaiti newspaper said on Thursday remarks by the United States over a possible arms deal with China should not be allowed to pass.
"The statement should not be allowed to pass quietly because it is dangerous...," a front page editorial in al-Rai al-Aam daily said.
State Department spokesman Nicholas Burns urged Kuwait on Tuesday to reject Chinese weapons and "buy American".

"We had a war (in 1991) to liberate Kuwait... We saved Kuwait. We saved the royal family. And we saved the economy and the structure of the society as Kuwait knows it. And we assume that Kuwait hasn't forgotten that," he told reporters.
Kuwait has not responded publicly to Burns's remarks.
The Kuwaiti daily said Burns appeared "as if he is our guardian or a teacher giving a lesson to naughty students".
"Washington is strange, it gets aroused by the possibility of making a deal with another party so it forgets that there are norms which govern dealing with countries even if they are small...".

Britain and the United States, both seeking to secure the deal for tracked self-propelled howitzers, have strongly advised Kuwait in private against the Chinese offer but have been careful to use softer language in public, diplomats said.
Both states played a leading role in freeing Kuwait in 1991 from a seven-month Iraqi occupation.

Experts earlier said that a Kuwaiti military committee had recommended the Chinese 155mm gun over the American M109 A6 Paladin, the British Desert AS90 and the South African LIW 155mm G6, the only offer for a wheeled system.
But Kuwait has said it has not signed any deal with China.
